checks.claim: EPA has said one gallon of gasoline can make about a million gallons of groundwater unusable.
checks.why: EPA releases give about one million gallons (later ones up to 5 million); 'about a million' is the conservative figure.

checks.claim: Leaking underground storage tanks have been a leading source of groundwater contamination in America.
checks.why: EPA called them the most common source in 1997; recent reporting says a leading cause.

sources.title: Beneath the surface - Christian Science Monitor

checks.claim: New or replaced US underground tanks must have secondary containment (double walls) with interstitial monitoring
checks.why: EPA's 2015 requirements page says exactly this, from April 11, 2016.

checks.claim: US underground storage tanks must have spill prevention equipment such as a spill bucket at the fill pipe
checks.why: EPA's release prevention page describes the spill bucket around the fill pipe as the required spill protection.
